drafted_from: tools/keep-and-wake-ai-sessions-on-this-computer/tool-rows.json (tool:set-up-trillion-hooks-in-an-ai-app-on-this-computer), harness/setup.mjs and test/harness-setup.test.mjs, and a run of setup() with a non-Mac platform over an empty scratch home
start_here: Say to your AI: "Inspect whether Trillion's hooks are set up in Claude Code on this computer, and change nothing." It runs the inspect action and tells you what is ready and what each failed check says.
no_lists_because: It reads and edits one AI app's own settings file on this computer and keeps no list of yours.
instructions: 1. Clone the Workshop checkout, run npm ci in its root, and pick the app: claude-code or codex.

2. Say "Inspect Trillion's hooks in claude-code". The AI reads the row with tools:list and runs node tools/keep-and-wake-ai-sessions-on-this-computer/harness/setup.mjs --action inspect --harness claude-code. inspect writes nothing.
3. Read the report: status, ready, checks (id, status, reason), changes and boundaries. Exit 0 means ready, 2 not ready, 1 a wrong request.

4. Only when you ask, run --action apply to add the hooks (your own settings and permissions are kept and a backup is made) or --action remove to take them out again. Applying never writes an MCP entry; connecting the app is a separate tool.

worked_examples.title: Inspect on a computer that is not a Mac
worked_examples.ask: Inspect whether Trillion's hooks are set up in Claude Code on this computer.
worked_examples.given: The command is node tools/keep-and-wake-ai-sessions-on-this-computer/harness/setup.mjs --action inspect --harness claude-code. Worked out by calling setup() from harness/setup.mjs with action inspect, harness claude-code, platform linux and an empty scratch home (the test "unknown hosts, unsupported platforms and disabled hooks" asserts the same unsupported platform check); on a real Mac the checks list is longer.
